request.text:
A: <Quiet, clear storyteller; intimate and grounded. Let the cave's silence linger. Mood: idle.> Ashmaw lowers its head. The sliver of the ford's fallen ember in the wall gutters once, then crumbles into grey dust. Nothing remains to sell or carry. A heavy claw rests warm against the stone.
<long pause>
A: Maud's kettle still whistles in the memory. 'It was thrown,' she said, and her old eyes saw more than anyone in town.
<long pause>
A: The thought returns with the smell of woodsmoke: the warmth was lent, not given. You look into the coals a little differently.
<long pause>
A: For three hundred years the Hearthflame burned in Ember Keep, and kept the whole Vale warm.
<long pause>
A: A century ago the Keep fell in a single night. The flame broke into five embers, and they came down across the Vale like stars. This is one of them.
<long pause>
A: Rook watches you lift the ember out of the riverbed, shrugs, and walks off into the dark. It sits warm in your pack.
<long pause>
A: Back in Emberwick, at the Last Coal, late. The common room is empty, and the hearth burns low on its old shard, red at the edges.
<long pause>
A: Emberwick's archive is two rooms above the chandler's, stacked to the rafters. Corvin Ashby, the town archivist, meets you at the door, very pale.
<long pause>
A: The door slides aside without a sound. Rows of bone Wardens stand at their posts, and on the dais, a necromancer is chanting.
<long pause>
A: A mason's note, in the margin: We were told to build a hearth. We have built a cage. Gods forgive us if the thing inside ever wakes and wants to go home.
<long pause>
A: Pip caught up with you at the foot of the pass, and walks at the front. Nobody agreed that she could come. Nobody managed to stop her, either.
<long pause>
A: The fourth ember is somewhere up in Frostpeak Pass, where the mountain froze around it seventy years ago.
<long pause>
A: Far away, the river at the ford boils once. What Rook left of its ember crosses the sky, smaller than a fist, and drops into the hall to join its sisters.
<long pause>
A: Far away, the river at the ford boils once and goes still. A light crosses the sky, and the ford's ember drops into the hall to join its sisters.
<long pause>
A: Around the flame lies a red dragon. It came for the heat a century ago, and has slept coiled around the heart ever since. As the chanting rises, one eye opens.
<long pause>
A: Oswin bends back over his ledger. Whatever else you came to ask, it will have to wait.
<long pause>
B: Though I would like to know why the mayor had my granaries shut so early. He never did say.
